golden.input: Reply with exactly the single word: ping. Output only that word, no punctuation, no explanation.
golden._note: Instruction-following echo. The stub lane echoes the whole input (contains 'ping' -> deterministic pass). A capable model returns 'ping' (pass); a model that adds chatter still contains 'ping'. The bench compares HOW each lane answers the same golden case, surfacing latency + tokens per model.

golden.input: Reply with exactly the single word: pong. Output only that word, no punctuation, no explanation.
golden._note: Second instruction-following echo so the bench has >1 case per model (perModel passRate is a rate, not a single coin-flip). Stub lane echoes input (contains 'pong'); the live model is judged on whether its text contains 'pong'.

golden.input: What is the capital of France? Answer with just the city name.
golden._note: A real knowledge question where the lanes DIVERGE honestly: the stub lane echoes the QUESTION text (which does not contain 'Paris') -> stub FAILS this case deterministically, while a capable live model answers 'Paris' -> PASSES. This makes the per-model passRate genuinely differ across lanes (the whole point of a multi-model bench), not a trivially-all-pass slice.
